headline: Broad Commodity Selloff Deepens Led by Heavy Losses in Metals
paragraphs: Silver led today's commodities decline, plunging 8.08% to $41.37 (EUR 37.68) per ounce under pressure from Federal Reserve interest rate expectations. Palladium tumbled 7.27% to $881.00 (EUR 802.50), gold dropped 5.72% to $3528.00 (EUR 3213.66), and platinum declined 4.87% to $1293.80 (EUR 1178.52). The precious metals complex faced widespread selling driven by dual highs in the US dollar and Treasury yields alongside rate hike expectations.

Natural gas retreated 3.50% to $3.25 (EUR 2.96) following a larger-than-average storage build. Copper dropped 2.77% to $5.50 (EUR 5.01) per pound as industry reports highlighted declining demand across industrial and speculative channels. Brent crude fell 2.39% to $89.75 (EUR 81.75) per barrel, compounding weekly energy losses; the exact reason for the daily drop is unclear given conflicting reports of Middle East tanker attacks and supply surplus outlooks.
